The Telegraph — published 30 September 2026, 12:56 BST (author Laura Donnelly)

GPs to be trained to spot domestic abuse

GPs will be trained to spot domestic abuse under Government plans to tackle violence against women.

Yvette Cooper, the Health Secretary, has announced almost £50m for services to help victims, warning that the NHS too often fails to address abuse behind women's ill health.

A new referral programme, called Steps to Safety, will enable patients to access specialist support through their GP.

Doctors and practice staff will be trained to recognise signs of abuse and sensitively ask patients about their experiences, helping identify those who might otherwise stay silent.

Ms Cooper told Labour's party conference in Liverpool that violence was "one of the biggest causes of ill health and harm for women, including in pregnancy".

Yet it "isn't really treated on the NHS", she said, adding: "We don't treat violence against women and girls as the epidemic it really is."

Of the funding announced for abuse victims, £34.4m will go to 12 integrated care boards to deliver the first phase of Steps to Safety. A further £15m will go towards victim support services across England.

Ms Cooper will also appoint a national clinical lead for violence against women and girls to strengthen the response across health services.
